title: An aging beauty
caption: The globular cluster NGC 6139, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6139 · constellation Scorpius · about 35000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This rich, dense smattering of stars is NGC 6139, a massive globular cluster that orbits the Milky Way, held together by its own gravity. It is seen roughly in the direction of our galaxy's centre, in the constellation of Scorpius, the Scorpion.

Globular clusters are denser and rounder than open clusters such as the well-known Pleiades. They usually hold hundreds of thousands of stars thought to have formed at about the same time. Studies show that NGC 6139 is home to an ageing population. Most globular clusters around the Milky Way are estimated to be more than 10 billion years old, so they contain some of our galaxy's oldest stars, formed very early in its history.
Even so, exactly what role these clusters played in how galaxies evolve is still being studied. Scorpius, a constellation full of fascinating objects, is a place Hubble has looked many times.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.61 x 1.33 arcminutes) and distance (35000 light years), the frame spans roughly 27 × 14 light-years. Its light set out about 35,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 imaged the cluster through blue and visual filters in visible light. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Hubble's sharp view separates individual stars in the cluster that the eye could not tell apart.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Among Hubble's other targets in Scorpius are the butterfly-shaped Bug Nebula, surprising binary star systems and other globular clusters. NGC 6139 lies about 35,000 light-years away.
alt: A rich, dense cluster of many stars.
